svg.title: The safety case on the V-cycle
svg.desc: The safety case on the V-cycle: 36 claims; 12 both sides of the V, 5 definition only, 5 verification only, 10 across the V, 3 through its sub-claims, 1 no evidence; 42 open defeaters.
svg.text: The safety case on the V-cycle
Every claim of the safety case (case-records), and the boxes of the V its evidence comes from: does each claim stand on both definition and verification?
Reference configuration poses no unreasonable risk
Limits enforced on every TX frame
No steering actuation while not engaged
Envelope faults reach the safe state in the FTTI
SG-02 lateral loss without warning is met
SG-05 release on driver action is met
SG-06 longitudinal loss without warning is met
SG-07 stock PCS preserved is met
QM SoC cannot interfere with the envelope
Credited assumptions of use are verified
Foreseeable misuse is detected or prevented
Actuation stays within a controllable envelope
Deployed models are the validated ones
Model input space covers the ODD
Degraded model behaviour is detected or bounded
Safety-relevant code and evidence under CM
Requirements traceable from SG to code and test
Reviews and confirmation at required independence
Tools and reused components are qualified
Operation keeps configuration and AoUs valid
No public-road operation outside the test regime
Circle: evidence items from that box (size = count), coloured by the furthest step reached:
A claim's evidence is its evidence_refs in case-records; an item's box is where it lives, as in evidence maturity. Drawing a claim does not review or accept it.

g.text: Terms: AI artificial intelligence · AIR-nn AI safety requirement (WP-C-11 §6) · AoU assumption of use: what the analysis assumes about the car, the driver or the environment · CM configuration management: identifying, baselining and controlling changes to work products (WP-P-01)

· FTTI fault-tolerant time interval: fault to hazard, the time a safety mechanism has · G0–G6 gate G0…G6 of the project lifecycle; in the safety case, a claim G0, G1, G1.1… (WP-K-01) · ISO International Organization for Standardization · ODD operational design domain: where the

system is meant to work · PAS publicly available specification (ISO/PAS 8800 is the AI safety one) · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning and braking · QM quality managed: no ASIL; ordinary quality processes suffice · SAE SAE International (formerly the

Society of Automotive Engineers) · SG-nn safety goal (HARA §6) · SoC system on chip: the comma device's main processor, running openpilot (QM) · SOTIF safety of the intended functionality (ISO 21448): hazards with nothing failing · TX transmit
